newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebels say civilians killed in Sri Lanka offensive.
newsitem.headline: Rebels say civilians killed in Sri Lanka offensive.

text.p: Separatist Tamil Tiger rebels launched a fierce attack on Sri Lankan troops advancing north along one flank as part of a major thrust into rebel territory on Thursday, military officials said.

Troops which advanced from the northern frontline town of Puvarasankulam met stiff resistance from Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) at Kuruvikulam, west of the government-held town of Vavuniya, on Thursday morning, they said.
A military official said at least 12 rebels were killed and more were believed wounded in the Kuruvikulam battle. The number of army casualties was uncertain, he added.
Meanwhile, soldiers which had advanced on another flank to capture the rebel-held town of Omanthai on Wednesday, were consolidating, the Defence Ministry said on Thursday.

Troops, backed by artillery, tanks and helicopter gunships, broke out of their bases in Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo on Tuesday, launching an offensive code-named "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", into the rebel-held northern Wanni heartland.

LTTE transmissions monitored by the army said at least 100 rebels had been killed or wounded in the battle for Omanthai, a Defence Ministry spokesman said. He said army casualties in Omanthai and elsewhere stood at 18 dead and 31 wounded in the three-day-old offensive.

LTTE rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.

Analysts said the aim of the fresh offensive was to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north. Vavuniya lies 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
The military has been tight-lipped about where the troops were heading.
But the LTTE's international spokesman in London accused the military of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their properties under the guise of opening up a supply route.
"Army artillery has been raining down on Tamil civilians and on their homes and in most cases they were nowhere near the supply route the army wants to open," Anton Raja told Reuters by telephone.
He said droves of civilians have begun to abandon their homes and seek shelter in mosquito-infested jungles.
"The Chandrika (Kumaratunga) government is blatantly violating a plea by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to protect civilians in war," Raja said.
The ICRC earlier this month appealed to the government and rebels to spare civilians and respect humanitarian law during times of war.

Military officials said LTTE positions in the Wanni region came under heavy attack on Thursday when the army fired shells from bases at Welioya, Kilinochchi and Elephant Pass in the north, officials said.
An international aid worker in Vavuniya told Reuters at least 10 civilians were killed and more had been wounded from the artillery shelling of Wanni.
But other aid workers said they had not seen large scale civilian movement as during previous offensives.
A large number of civilians, anticipating the offensive, had already moved to safer locations, they said.
